title: Coroner's inquest scheduled into 2020 death of man after transfer from P.A. police custody to hospital
subtitle: The inquest in the death of Jordan Norfield is scheduled to take place June 26 to June 30 in Prince Albert.
article: A coroner's inquest has been set for June in the 2020 death of 30-year-old Jordan Norfield, who died after he was transferred from the Prince Albert Police Service's custody to Victoria Hospital.
The inquest is scheduled to be held from June 26-30 at the Coronet Hotel in Prince Albert, with lawyer Timothy Hawryluk serving as the presiding coroner.
Norfield died at Prince Albert's Victoria Hospital on Dec. 5, 2020 after he had been transferred there from the police's custody by ambulance, according to a provincial news release on Friday.

In a media release issued at the time, Prince Albert police said the man had been taken into custody on Dec. 1, 2020 on a detention order under the provincial Public Health Act . He was put in police detention cells overnight, police said.

Police said in the previous release that the following morning, the man was taken to Victoria Hospital for assessment and treatment and they were later told the man had died in hospital on Dec. 5, 2020.

Inquests are a public fact-finding, not fault-finding, process that establishes who died, when and how. The process may also highlight dangerous conditions or practices, and the six-member jury can make non-binding recommendations.

Under The Coroners Act, the chief coroner shall hold an inquest into the death of a person who dies while they are an inmate at a jail or correctional facility unless the coroner is satisfied the death was entirely due to natural causes and wasn't preventable.
